title: Native Trino S3 client struggles under load, AWS Client is fine in Trino 464
body:
Hi Team,

We are operating relatively large Trino clusters consistently under heavy load, typically running 50-60 concurrent queries that may execute for hours. After upgrading from Trino 419 to Trino 464, we've observed significant query stalls.

Initially, we encountered issues with indefinite TCP connection timeouts. Setting appropriate timeouts resolved this issue, and the cluster performed well under light load.

However, under heavy utilization, another problem emerged. After about 15-20 minutes of running the adjusted cluster, we noticed some SQL queries hanging indefinitely without any observable activity. After experimenting with various settings, switching to the Legacy S3 connector restored normal behavior.

After digging into the state of JVM it appears that there are a lot of hanging http processes, which suggest that something is not right with the network connection pooling.

Let me know what debug information you would need for this.

Thanks

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant1 if I may chip in, we noticed a regression in cluster performance (with fault tolerance on task level enabled, S3) when several queries are launched that read a lot of input data (1TB+). This has two implications:
- S3 throttling kicks in for this queries - we use 6 buckets rn, but when I changed it to 45 buckets, queries become "stuck" after just 10 minutes of cluster uptime
- Node network saturates (that's a theory - might be wrong) - at least we see that transmitting data for joins slows down by a mile

This was on Trino 466. I've rolled back from 45 exchange buckets to 6 and from 466 to 465, and things got back to normal - minus when S3 throttle activates, queries get slowed down for a short period.

Cluster runs m6in.4xlarge for coordinator and 6x m7g.12xlarge nodes for workers with 128 GB XmX / 160GB worker node container

comments.author: participant3

@participant2 Between 465 and 466 the only related change seems to be updating AWS SDK from 2.29.16 to 2.29.21.

Might be worth checking changes between those. The original issue is however comparing between Legacy FS (Hadoop S3 implementation using AWS SDK v1) and Native FS (direct usage of AWS SDK v2).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 I am currently Running Trino 470 with Trino native S3 connector and the issue appears to be gone. On the flip side, Hadoop S3 connector is giving a lot of headache instead (which is being discontinued), so I switched to the native one hoping the issue is addressed and it is. The issue was heavily amplified by unmaintained Iceberg tables with millions of tiny files. Would be nice to have some warnings about such tables in the logs.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Posting this, initially posted in #6405, which is now closed, here:

I have experienced the same issue, even with Express One Buckets, which have very big rate limits, which suggests the issue is on Trino's side. In addition, I also see that downloads of data files from S3 are quite slow. This would suggest that there is some issue with the download and write speed to S3 inside the Trino and the reason why adding more buckets solves it for the Exchange operator is that there are more copies of an internal resource that deals with each individual bucket.

> @participant1 if I may chip in, we noticed a regression in cluster performance (with fault tolerance on task level enabled, S3) when several queries are launched that read a lot of input data (1TB+). This has two implications:
> 
> S3 throttling kicks in for this queries - we use 6 buckets rn, but when I changed it to 45 buckets, queries become "stuck" after just 10 minutes of cluster uptime
Node network saturates (that's a theory - might be wrong) - at least we see that transmitting data for joins slows down by a mile
This was on Trino 466. I've rolled back from 45 exchange buckets to 6 and from 466 to 465, and things got back to normal - minus when S3 throttle activates, queries get slowed down for a short period.

> Cluster runs m6in.4xlarge for coordinator and 6x m7g.12xlarge nodes for workers with 128 GB XmX / 160GB worker node container

We get this issue without apparent S3 slowdowns. Furthermore, we stop getting the issue with 6 standard S3 buckets. But 1 express one bucket already has more rate limits than 6 standard buckets and still fails (and works fine with 6 express one buckets). This makes us think that the issue is not related to S3 rate-limits. Furthermore, a simple test using multiple threads to download data from S3 allows us to download at much bigger speeds than what Trino is achieving. Hence, it is also not probably a node network issue (plus, we use nodes with much guaranteed network bandwidth than what we achieve.) I would be inclined to think the issue is on Trino's side.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Hey all, we are facing the same issue in Trino 478 and the Iceberg Connector. Minio responds with rate limiting codes and the S3 client adapts and slows down entirely.

While the mechanism as such if fine and the problem lied in the not maintained iceberg tables with a lot of files what seems to be a bug IMO is the Trino S3 client capability to return to the default rate. After problematic query that triggers the rate limitter Trino cluster needs a restart to come back to the default state.

I don't think there is sufficient information here for anyone to debug and it seems everyone is talking about different scenarios with common theme of S3 throttling.
Since the original reporter's issue is no longer reproducible https://github.com/trinodb/trino/issues/24282#issuecomment-3068957209, I'm closing this. New reports can be tackled as separate GH issues.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I finally managed to find a reason for this problem.
It turns out that S3 client pool that is used for iceberg connectors is different from the pool used for exchange and therefore also has different configuration properties.
The error is related to how Trino handles the 429 Too Many Requests response.

Any error is handled by s3.retry-mode strategy :

https://<redacted-host>/blogs/developer/announcing-updated-retry-behavior-for-aws-sdks-and-tools/
https://<redacted-host>/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-retry-behavior.html

For iceberg connectors the default is LEGACY -> STANDARD and therefore this can recover from slowdown but somehow for exchange the client is set to ADAPTIVE strategy that increases the backoff every time up to infinity.
When Trino is under pressure and exchange S3 client receives 429 response Trino eventually would exchaust the connection pool as many connections would stale for hours waiting for retry:

```
2026-06-18T13:00:12.054Z        DEBUG   SplitRunner-20260618_130011_00005_xwrrq.7.0.0-95-2725   software.amazon.awssdk.request  Retryable error detected. Will retry in 60000ms. Request attempt number 1
2026-06-18T13:00:12.054Z        DEBUG   SplitRunner-20260618_130011_00005_xwrrq.7.0.0-87-2717   software.amazon.awssdk.request  Retryable error detected. Will retry in 60000ms. Request attempt number 1
2026-06-18T13:00:12.054Z        DEBUG   SplitRunner-20260618_130011_00005_xwrrq.7.0.0-83-2713   software.amazon.awssdk.request  Retryable error detected. Will retry in 60000ms. Request attempt number 1
2026-06-18T13:00:12.054Z        DEBUG   SplitRunner-20260618_130011_00005_xwrrq.7.0.0-89-2719   software.amazon.awssdk.request  Retryable error detected. Will retry in 60000ms. Request attempt number 1
```

The solution was not to use ADAPTATIVE strategy for the exchange bucket handling.

```
exchange.s3.retry-mode=STANDARD
```

I am really not sure why Trino used different defaults for S3 clients for Iceberg connector and different for exchange bucket. Perhaps it should be changed or better documented as this can cause hours of slowdown.
